title: Produce sub_agent acceptance evaluations, or report the gap before the request, when a project's policy admits sub_agent
outcome:
TermAl's host does not produce sub_agent evaluations. src/acceptance_evaluation_api.rs:887-890 answers 501 "the task or its policy requires a sub_agent evaluation, which this host does not produce yet", and project settings refuse sub_agent as a default (src/acceptance_settings.rs:26).
The failing path: with no pin, select_acceptance_evaluation_mode (src/acceptance_evaluation.rs:94-109) takes the first admitted mode in the order independent_session, sub_agent, same_session. Engram policies may admit [sub_agent, same_session] or [sub_agent] alone (Engram::Coder, TermAl mailbox 62e0c56d #47). Such a project therefore gets 501 on every unpinned request.
Falling back to same_session is ruled out. Engram's planned rule (Engram w-a5f404605e07, revision 7) rejects unpinned same_session whenever another mode is admitted, and a silent fallback would permit self-evaluation.
The fix is one of:
(a) produce sub_agent evaluations as Engram defines them;
(b) until then, report the capability gap where a project's policy is read (settings and readiness), so a request isn't the first place it shows.
acceptance: A sub_agent evaluation TermAl produces is submitted by a distinct child session under its own session id, never the parent's, with the executor as parent_session; a test shows that the submission's evaluator session is none of the run's holder, executor or former holders.

sub_agent is produced; the project's acceptance settings offer it as an available mode, the 'not produced' warning and disabled option are removed; a test covers each admitted-list case showing the selected mode.

With a project policy admitting [sub_agent, same_session] or [sub_agent] and no pin, an evaluation request never falls back to same_session: it either produces a sub_agent evaluation that Engram accepts, or refuses with a reason naming the capability gap; and a task pinned to sub_agent under a policy that admits it gets the same outcome. Engram's acceptance is shown by a pinned disposable-Engram run through the `live` launcher with the stable pin, on the real host submission path: one positive case recorded as sub_agent, and one producer refusal that the host's preflight does not pre-empt, surfaced as final; mocked receipts do not establish it.
